Grow as summer bedding in any moist but well-drained soil in full sun or as a container plant under glass where it needs light but shade from direct sunlight
Grow in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade
Grow in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Propagate by seed in situ in spring or early autumn; self seeds freely in a sunny position
Grow in any well-drained fertile soil in full sun
Grow in any well-drained fertile soil in full sun
Grow in any well-drained fertile soil in full sun

Grow in moderately fertile, neutral to alkaline, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil in full sun
Grow in moderately fertile, well-drained soil in an open sunny position; thrives in alkaline soil. A bushy perennial to 80cm tall with violet-blue, yellow-centred flowers from summer into autumn.
Grow in gritty, poor to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. A strong-growing corm with large, bright orange-yellow flowers in spring.

notes: Grow in sun or shade in moist but well-drained soil; good in damp shade. Clump-forming perennial to 60cm with brownish-pink reflexed flowers, late spring to early summer.
Grow in humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil that does not dry out in summer. Robust hybrid snowdrop, around 20cm tall, flowering late winter to spring.

Grow in light, moderately fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil in full sun; can tolerate light partial shade. Compact bushy perennial with deep violet-blue flower spikes, summer into autumn. Cut back spent spikes to prolong flowering.
Grow in a well-drained, sunny position; plant corms 5-6cm deep in late summer or early autumn. Reddish-purple flowers with a bright orange stigma. Suitable for naturalising in grass.
Grow in moderately fertile, light, well-drained soil; sandy soil is ideal, full sun essential. Vigorous perennial to 60-90cm with violet-purple flowers; often seeds freely.

Grow in any well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; may need support. Bushy perennial with light violet-blue flowers, summer into early autumn. Trim after flowering to keep compact and encourage reflowering.
Grow in moderately fertile, well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Drought-tolerant upright perennial to 60cm with dense clusters of starry pale pink flowers.

notes: Grow in sun or shade in well-drained soil; excellent ground-cover, low maintenance, no pruning required. Mat-forming evergreen perennial with aromatic foliage and warm pink flowers, early to midsummer.
Grow in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil; best in containers where soil is heavy clay. Bulbous perennial to 35cm with pinkish-lilac star-shaped flowers in domed clusters, early summer.

Grow in any moist soil in full sun or partial shade. Vigorous native perennial to 1.5m that can spread quickly; very attractive to butterflies and other pollinating insects. Late summer into early autumn flowering.

Grow in any moderately fertile soil, including heavy clay, in sun or partial shade. Tall native biennial to 2.5m with bristly flowerheads; seedheads attract goldfinches over winter. Propagates by seed sown in situ.

Prefers a sunny site and slightly acid, low-nitrogen soil; naturally occurs in grassland. Native perennial to 50cm with pinkish-red flowers, May to October; a great nectar source, especially for bees. Generally pest and disease-free.

Tolerates most soils; needs sun to flower and fruit well. Vigorous native thorny scrambler, spread wider than 8m, valuable for wildlife but can become a nuisance if unmanaged; needs regular hard pruning, cutting old canes and shortening new ones, sometimes to ground level every few years.

Grows in any moist but well-drained soil in sun or partial shade; ideal for naturally peaty soil. Native clump-forming perennial to 60cm with pale violet pincushion-like flowerheads. No pruning required, generally disease-free. HOST PLANT to the small scabious mining bee

Grows in grassy places in sun on well-drained, low-nitrogen soils; often appears in lawns. Native perennial with yellow pea flowers, late spring to early autumn. No pruning required, generally pest and disease-free.

Easy to grow in any soil, full sun or partial shade. Native creeping ground-cover perennial; may be considered invasive, deadhead to prevent excessive self-seeding. Attracts bees and other beneficial insects.

Grows in almost any soil, avoiding very wet or dry sites; prefers humus-rich soil in partial shade but tolerates full sun. Native biennial to 2m, freely self-sowing. CAUTION: toxic if eaten, toxic to pets; wear gloves when handling.

Happy in a wide range of conditions, prefers rich soil; naturally found in grassy places and waste ground. Bright yellow flowers, April to June, followed by wind-dispersed seed heads. No pruning required, generally pest and disease-free.

Grow in poor, moist soil in full sun. Vigorous rhizomatous perennial, spreads far and wide with potential to become a nuisance — RHS recommends planting in deep containers plunged into the soil. Cut back at end of growing season.

Easy to grow in most well-drained, alkaline to neutral soils in full sun. Bushy evergreen sub-shrub to 20cm with lemon-scented leaves and pale lilac flowers. Drought resistant, generally pest and disease-free.

Grow in poor to moderately fertile, well-drained, preferably alkaline soil in full sun; protect from winter wet. Trailing semi-evergreen sub-shrub with pale purple flowers and showy pink bracts over a long period. Generally pest and disease-free.

Grow in well-drained soil in a sheltered, sunny position. Compact evergreen shrub with fragrant deep purple flower spikes, mid to late summer. Drought resistant. Needs annual trimming to prevent legginess; avoid cutting into old wood.

Prefers well-drained neutral to alkaline soil, tolerates acidic conditions; avoid waterlogging. High-nitrogen fertiliser causes floppy growth. Evergreen shrub to 90cm with deep bluish-purple, very aromatic flower spikes. Drought resistant. Avoid cutting into old wood when pruning.

Grow in fertile, well-drained, alkaline to neutral soil in full sun. Compact spreading sub-shrub with blue flower spikes, summer into early autumn. Needs pruning group 10 treatment (structured spring pruning) to keep shape.

Easy to grow in most well-drained, alkaline to neutral soils in full sun; good for rock gardens or paving crevices. Low mat-forming evergreen sub-shrub with flesh-pink flowers, releases fragrance when trodden on. Cut back hard after flowering. Generally pest and disease-free.

Grow in poor to moderately fertile, well-drained soil in sun. Bushy evergreen shrub, 15cm to 2m tall depending on selection, with pale violet-blue flowers. CAUTION: skin allergen, wear gloves when handling. Needs pruning group 9 treatment, trim hedges after flowering.

Grow in any well-drained soil in sun or part shade. Rounded shrub to 2m with sweetly-scented cream-white flowers on bare branches, winter into early spring. CAUTION: ornamental berries, not edible. Pruning group 2.

Grow in full sun or part shade, fertile humus-rich moist but well-drained soil; feed and mulch in late winter/spring for best flowering. Vigorous shrub rose to 2.5m, once-flowering scarlet-orange blooms followed by red hips. Susceptible to blackspot, rust, mildew and multiple pests. Specific pruning timing: do not prune after flowering if hips wanted.

Grow in any well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, sheltered from cold winds. Vigorous arching shrub to 5m with white flowers followed by yellow berries turning pink. CAUTION: ornamental berries, not edible. Pruning group 8, only if necessary.

Grow in any deep moist well-drained soil in full sun; dislikes shallow chalk soils. Large native shrub or small tree, 8-12m tall, with silvery-grey catkins in spring before leaves. Reaches proper tree scale — needs real long-term space commitment. Pruning group 1 (light). HOST PLANT to Clarke's mining bee

Good for woodland settings, sheltered or exposed, full sun or partial shade. Upright evergreen shrub to 4m with fragrant yellow flower racemes, late autumn into winter. Generally pest and disease-free. CAUTION: ornamental berries, not edible. Pruning group 8.

notes: Tolerant of most soils and conditions; grows best in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained alkaline soil, sheltered. Grow in any well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, sheltered from cold winds. Arching evergreen/semi-evergreen shrub to 5m with white flowers, apricot-yellow fruits. CAUTION: ornamental berries, not edible. Pruning group 8, only if necessary.

Easy to grow in fertile soil, sun or partial shade; tolerant of pollution. Large spiny evergreen shrub to 2.5m, white flowers followed by long-lasting orange berries. CAUTION: spiny/thorny, ornamental berries not edible. Pruning group 1 (light).

Grow in a container of peat-free loam-based compost with grit, full light, shade from hot sun. Water freely and mist daily in growth; water sparingly in winter. Feed year-round with citrus fertiliser. Cannot survive frost — must overwinter under glass every year without fail. Susceptible to red spider mite, scale, aphids, mealybugs under glass.

notes: Grow in any but very dry soil. Has the potential to become a nuisance if not managed well. To restrict growth, cut back hard in early spring.

Spreads readily over time, often wandering through borders via suckers, and any root fragment left behind regrows - allocate and monitor for containment, not the young-plant size. Dislikes being moved once established. CAUTION: mild irritant if ingested/handled.

RHS-listed Plants for Pollinators. Occurs naturally in damp places on rich soils, poorly-drained clay or loam. Hairy perennial forming clumps by creeping rhizomes; may be cut back at end of season. Generally pest and disease-free. HOST PLANT for the yellow loosestrife bee (Macropis europaea), a specialist that collects both pollen and floral oils from this plant to waterproof its nest cells.

RHS-listed Plants for Pollinators. Suitable for rock gardens, sunny walls, banks, or containers. No pruning required. Susceptible to slugs, snails, aphids; may get rust or powdery mildew. HOST PLANT for the harebell carpenter bee (Chelostoma campanularum) and other Campanula-specialist bees, which collect pollen almost exclusively from this genus.
